capturedFrom: the original T-SQL object, deployed unchanged to a scratch SQL Server database with the fixed case's rows
review: Captured from the source engine, not derived independently. A reviewer checks each case's expected values against its label at step 5 (second review). Values are canonical: n: number, s: text, b: bit, d: date, t: timestamp (microseconds), x: bytes (hex), ∅: NULL.

cases.label: [A01] order instant 1 ms after the end date (.001): SQL Server rounds the datetime argument to .000, inside the period
[A02] order instant 1 ms before the start date (.999): SQL Server rounds it up to the start, inside the period
[A03] StartDate stored as .001 (datetime keeps .000) and an order instant at .000: inside the period on SQL Server
[A04] EndDate stored as 23:59:59.999 (datetime rounds to the next midnight) and an order instant at that midnight
[A05] EndDate stored as .002 (datetime keeps .003) and an order instant at .003
[A06] StartDate stored as half a millisecond (.0005) and an order instant at .000
[A07] a period starting on 1753-01-01 (datetime minimum), order instant at that minimum, value 0.0005: the ListPrice
[A08] open-ended period on 9999-12-31 00:00 exactly (the COALESCE end, inclusive): the ListPrice
[A09] open-ended period on 9999-12-31 23:59:59.997 (after the COALESCE end at midnight): NULL
[A10] an explicit EndDate at the datetime maximum (9999-12-31 23:59:59.997), order instant equal to it: the ListPrice
[A11] a value with 5 decimals (10.00005) rounds to money's 4 places on load: the ListPrice
[A12] a negative value at the last place (-0.0005): the ListPrice
[A14] the money maximum 922337203685477.5807 passes through unchanged
[A15] product keys with gaps (10, 20, 2147483647): the int-maximum product's ListPrice
[A16] a one-instant period (StartDate = EndDate = 12:34:56.789) and an order instant equal to it
[A17] an inverted period (EndDate before StartDate) and an order instant between them: NULL
[A18] a period starting at 08:00 on 2020-01-01 and an order instant at midnight that day: NULL
[A19] a product whose only period ended, with the queried instant in a later year and a different product's period covering it: NULL
